surfaceForm: The campus fabric is partitioned at layer~2 into \gls{vlan}s per zone ... / "the campus footprint" / "a campus-perimeter enclave" / "the open campus-scale reference"
location: ch08-network-EN.tex, \S Reference instantiation (sec:nw-reference, instantiationbox) and \S Functional role (operational considerations)
proposedGenericDecision: Treat the deployment substrate as one-or-more sites/fabrics, not a single campus. A role-based framing ("the institution's network fabric(s)") avoids assuming a single physical campus with one perimeter; multi-site / multi-campus institutions are common.
rationale: The instantiation and surrounding prose repeatedly presuppose a single 'campus fabric' with one enterprise perimeter. This is an implicit topology assumption that excludes multi-campus or distributed institutions; the contract itself (sec:nw-contract) explicitly disclaims topology, so the body text should match by speaking of 'fabric(s)/site(s)'.

surfaceForm: For an R1 institution, three to five engineers shared with adjacent duties is an indicative envelope; actual figures vary with the campus footprint and the research-network mission.
proposedGenericDecision: Express staffing as a role-based, size-relative range tied to a named scaling driver (network footprint + research-data mission) rather than an absolute 3-5 FTE pinned to a US Carnegie 'R1' classification. 'R1' is a US-specific taxonomy that does not transpose to non-US systems.
rationale: Both the 'R1' classifier (a Carnegie/US construct) and the concrete 3-5 engineer figure are jurisdiction-/scale-bound and read as a specific instantiation. Already softened by 'indicative' and 'actual figures vary', but the absolute number and US tier label still localise the claim.

surfaceForm: ESnet (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory); Stanford SUNet; CERN at the experimental boundaries
location: ch08-network-EN.tex, \S Reference instantiation -> realworldbox[ESnet Science DMZ and SUNet] (sec:nw-reference)
proposedGenericDecision: These are named institutional precedents used as illustrative anchors (role: 'a national research-network lab where the Science DMZ pattern originated'; 'a large research university operating multi-zone architecture'). They are not the authoring institution and the box already hedges ('should be verified ... before being cited'). Keep as evidence-layer precedents but ensure the surrounding architecture text never presents them as the institution's own deployment.
rationale: ESnet, Stanford/SUNet and CERN are third-party named exemplars (Layer-5 institutional precedents), not the home institution. They support institution-agnosticism by showing the pattern across organisations rather than tying it to one. Flagged for completeness but the recommended action is to retain them as precedents.

surfaceForm: GÉANT / \gls{geant}; ESnet; Internet2; CERN; LHCOPN; LHCONE; WLCG; perfSONAR; the LHC community / experiment-operated paths
location: ch08-network-EN.tex, \S Functional role; \S Reference instantiation (European and NREN-operated realisations paragraph + realworldbox[CERN LHCOPN/LHCONE and GÉANT]); zone catalogue table (perfSONAR)
proposedGenericDecision: Named NRENs, backbones, experiments and tools cited as generic realisations of the research-data-path contract function ('an NREN-operated dedicated circuit', 'a measurement tool', 'an experiment-operated overlay'). GÉANT/Internet2/ESnet/CERN are pan-/multi-national, not nation- or institution-specific, and perfSONAR is a generic tool name. These broaden rather than narrow applicability; keep as cited realisations.
rationale: These are cross-border research-infrastructure names presented explicitly as alternative realisations of the same contract ('satisfied by any of them'). They do not bind the document to the University of Luxembourg or to Luxembourg. Retain as generic, cited exemplars.

surfaceForm: Cisco, Juniper, Aruba, Arista (Alt.1); VMware NSX, Illumio, Cisco ACI, Cilium ClusterMesh (Alt.2); Cloudflare, Zscaler, Netskope (SASE); FreeRADIUS, Open vSwitch, Cilium (reference)
location: ch08-network-EN.tex, \S Alternative~1 (sec:nw-alt1), \S Alternative~2 (sec:nw-alt2), \S Discussion SASE/ZTNA (sec:nw-sase), \S Reference instantiation (sec:nw-reference)
proposedGenericDecision: Commercial and open product names used as category exemplars (role: 'proprietary macro-segmentation gear', 'commercial micro-segmentation overlay', 'SASE/ZTNA supplier', 'open attachment/overlay component'). They are technology choices, not institution identity, and are framed as illustrative classes ('such as', 'or'). Keep; they do not impede institution-agnostic reuse.
rationale: Vendor/product names denote technology alternatives any institution may evaluate; they carry no UL/Luxembourg binding. Recorded for completeness; no generalisation needed for agnosticism.

proposedGenericDecision: NIS2 is an EU Directive that binds entities only via national transposition; citing its articles as operative obligations implicitly assumes an EU member-state jurisdiction (and a national transposition) without naming the country. For a jurisdiction-agnostic suite, frame NIS2 as 'where the EU NIS2 Directive (as nationally transposed) applies' so non-EU adopters are not silently assumed in or out.
rationale: Directives (unlike GDPR, a directly-applicable Regulation) require national transposition; invoking NIS2 articles as binding presupposes an EU jurisdiction with a transposition in force. GDPR/ISO/NIST CSF references in the same paragraph are jurisdiction-neutral, so only the NIS2 framing carries the implicit-transposition assumption.

surfaceForm: the canonical TAC event schema / a TAC-aware attachment service
location: ch08-network-EN.tex, \S Discussion SASE/ZTNA -> Zero-Trust anchoring (sec:nw-sase); \S Reference instantiation -> Operational considerations (sec:nw-reference)
proposedGenericDecision: 'TAC' is an internal framework/house acronym of this document suite rather than a UL-institution identifier. Verify it is suite-defined (architecture term) and not an institution-specific system name; if suite-canonical, keep, ensuring it is glossary-defined so a reusing institution understands it as the architecture's event schema, not a UL product.
rationale: TAC appears to be the suite's own canonical event-schema/architecture concept (cross-layer), not a University of Luxembourg proper noun. Flagged only to confirm it is a portable framework term defined in the glossary rather than an institution-bound system name; no change expected if suite-canonical.
